concepts.title: Collecting and Organising Data
concepts.definition: Raw data, like a list of favourite colours or measured weights, becomes useful only when organised: counting how many times each value occurs and writing the results in a table prepares data for any graph.
concepts.key_idea: Organised data speaks: tables turn a jumble of facts into counts that can be compared.

how do we organise raw data using tally marks
why is organised data easier to read
make a frequency table of your classmates' favourite fruits
which value occurs most often in the given list
what questions can you answer from an organised table

concepts.title: Pictographs and Their Keys
concepts.definition: A pictograph shows data with pictures or symbols, where each symbol stands for a fixed number of things; reading the key first, then counting symbols and multiplying, gives every value.
concepts.key_idea: The key is the heart of a pictograph: without knowing what one symbol stands for, no count is possible.

concepts.title: Totals from a Frequency Table
concepts.definition: Once data sits in a table of counts, adding the row counts gives the total of all observations, a first step before drawing graphs or answering questions about the whole collection.
concepts.key_idea: The grand total is one addition away: row counts added together tell the size of the whole data set.
question_patterns: find the total number of children from the given table
how do you find the total from a table of counts
add the row counts of the given data table
what does the total tell us about the survey
check the total of your class survey table
why should the total match the number of responses

solution_steps.explain: Take the number written in every row of the table.
The sum of the row counts is the grand total.

concepts.title: Bar Graphs and Reading Them
concepts.definition: A bar graph shows data as bars of different heights on a common scale: taller bars mean bigger values, and the scale on the axis converts bar height back into numbers.
concepts.key_idea: Bar graphs trade pictures for lengths: equal spacing and a clear scale make comparison instant.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A table shows 12 children liked red, 8 liked blue and 5 liked green. Find the total number of children.

solution_template.explain: Take the numbers written against each row of the table.
The total is the sum of all the row counts.

worked_examples.question_pattern: In a survey, 15 houses have 1 pet, 9 houses have 2 pets and 6 houses have 3 pets. Add the counts of all rows.

solution_template.explain: Collect the three numbers from the table.
Adding them gives the grand total of houses.
